unit.unitTitle: Food and Drink: I Like, I Do Not Like

cefr.bandName: Pre-A1, from no English at all

unit.unitOverview:
Name food and drink.
Say I like and I do not like.
Say what you want.
Ask how much a thing costs.
unit.learningPath:
Listen to the lesson.
Words: food and drink.
Patterns: I like, I do not like, I want.
Listen to three short texts.
Order something. Record it.
Write about what you eat.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
functions: Say what you like and do not like
Ask for food or a drink
Say you are hungry or thirsty
Ask how much a thing costs

visual.lectureScript:
This is Unit 10. Today, food and drink.
First, food. Listen.
Bread. Rice. Egg. Meat. Fish. Fruit.
Say them with me. Bread. Rice. Egg.
Meat. Fish. Fruit.
Now drink. Water. Tea. Coffee. Milk.
Say them with me.
Now a new sentence. I like.
I like tea. I like fish.
Say it with me. I like.
And now the other side.
I do not like coffee.
Listen again. I do not like.
Three words. Do. Not. Like.
This is new. Until now you said no.
Now you can say a whole sentence.
Say it with me. I do not like.
Next, want. Want is not like.
I like tea, but now I want water.
Like is always. Want is now.
And in a shop or a cafe:
I want a cup of tea, please.
Or better: I would like a cup of tea.
Last, two feelings.
I am hungry. I want food.
I am thirsty. I want a drink.
And the question: How much is it?
That is Unit 10. Go and order a tea.

readings.setting: A small kitchen, in the evening
readings.passageScript:
In the morning I eat bread.
I drink tea with milk.
I do not like coffee.
At one o'clock I am hungry.
I eat rice and fish.
In the evening I eat bread again.
I drink water.
I like fruit, so I eat fruit every day.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: I like, I do not like
grammar.explanation:
Until now you answered no.
Now you can say a whole sentence.
I do not like takes three small words.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
I like tea.
I do not like coffee.

You like fish.
You do not like meat.

He likes rice.    (he, she, it → likes)
He does not like fish.
grammar.workedExample:
You are given coffee and you do not want it.
1. Start: I.
2. Then do not.
3. Then like.
4. Then the thing: coffee.
5. Say: I do not like coffee. Thank you.
grammar.commonMistake:
No: I not like coffee.
English needs do.
Yes: I do not like coffee.
Short form: I don't like coffee.
grammar.practice:
Make it negative.
1. I like fish. ___
2. I like coffee. ___
3. I like meat. ___
4. I like sugar in tea. ___
grammar.answerKey:
1. I do not like fish.
2. I do not like coffee.
3. I do not like meat.
4. I do not like sugar in tea.
All four? You can refuse politely now.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: Like and want are not the same
grammar.explanation:
Like is about always.
Want is about now.
Learners mix them, and it matters.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
I like tea.        (always, in general)
I want tea.        (now, today)

I like coffee, but I want water now.

In a cafe you say want or would like.
Not: I like a tea.
grammar.workedExample:
You are in a cafe and you are thirsty.
1. You are asking for now, not always.
2. So use want or would like.
3. Say: I would like a cup of tea, please.
4. Not: I like a cup of tea.
5. That would mean tea in general.
grammar.commonMistake:
No: I like a tea, please.
Yes: I would like a tea, please.
The word a is the clue: a means one, now.
grammar.practice:
Like or want?
1. In a cafe: I ___ a coffee, please.
2. In general: I ___ coffee.
3. I am thirsty. I ___ water.
4. Fish is good. I ___ fish.
grammar.answerKey:
1. want (or would like)
2. like
3. want
4. like
All four? This is a mistake worth not making.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: Ordering, and asking the price
grammar.explanation:
Two sentences carry a whole cafe.
One to ask. One to check the price.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
I would like a cup of tea, please.
A glass of water, please.

How much is it?
How much are they?

It is two.
Thank you.
grammar.workedExample:
You are at a counter and you want tea.
1. Say: I would like a tea, please.
2. They make it.
3. Ask: How much is it?
4. Listen to the number.
5. Not sure? Ask: Sorry, two or twelve?
grammar.commonMistake:
Do not point and say nothing.
One polite sentence is enough.
And always ask the price before you pay.
grammar.memoryTip: Please goes at the end of the ask.
grammar.practice:
Order these.
1. a tea
2. a glass of water
3. some bread
4. two eggs
grammar.answerKey:
Any polite form is right.
I would like a tea, please. is a good model.
Check: please in all four?
Bread takes some. Eggs take a number.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: I am hungry. I am thirsty.
grammar.explanation:
English says you ARE hungry.
Many languages say you HAVE hunger.
That is why this one needs saying.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
I am hungry.
I am thirsty.
I am tired.

Are you hungry?
Yes, I am.
No, I am not.
grammar.workedExample:
Your body wants food.
1. In English that is an adjective.
2. So use am, not have.
3. Say: I am hungry.
4. Then ask for what you need.
5. Say: I am hungry. Is there any bread?
grammar.commonMistake:
No: I have hungry.
No: I have hunger.
Yes: I am hungry.
grammar.memoryTip: Hungry and thirsty take am, not have.
grammar.practice:
Write am or have.
1. I ___ hungry.
2. I ___ a cup of tea.
3. I ___ thirsty.
4. I ___ some bread.
5. I ___ tired.
grammar.answerKey:
1. am
2. have
3. am
4. have
5. am
Four or five right? Feelings take am. Things take have.

3. A: Anything to eat? B: Some bread, please.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — I am hungry
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:

1. I am hungry.
2. I am thirsty.
3. I am not hungry.
4. Are you hungry?
5. Are you thirsty?
6. I am hungry. Is there any bread?

speaking.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
speaking.title: Speaking 6 — The sound in eat and it
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
Two sounds that learners mix.
Listen.
eat ... it ... eat ... it
Eat is long. It is short.
Now these pairs.
sheep ... ship
seat ... sit
Now say: I eat it.
Tap the mic. Say it three times.
Check: is the first sound longer than the last?

writing.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
writing.title: Writing 1 — What I eat
writing.promptAndInstructions:
Write four lines about your food.
Say what you eat and drink.
Use I like and I do not like.
writing.modelText:
In the morning I eat bread.
I drink tea with milk.
I do not like coffee.
I like fruit.
writing.successCriteria:
Four lines.
Use I like once, and I do not like once.
Each line starts with a capital.
Each line ends with a full stop.
writing.extension: Add a line about what you eat in the evening.

writing.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
writing.title: Writing 2 — A shopping list
writing.promptAndInstructions:
Write a list of six things to buy.
One on each line.
Put a number or the word some before each one.
writing.modelText:
some bread
two eggs
some rice
one fish
some milk
some fruit
writing.successCriteria:
Six things.
One on each line.
A number or some before each one.
They are all food or drink.
writing.extension: Now write how much you think it will cost.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.noteType: The first negative the learner builds
teacherNotes.note: Until now they have answered no. I do not like is the first time they make a negative sentence themselves, and the extra word do has no equivalent in most first languages. Expect I not like for a while and keep correcting it kindly.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.noteType: Like and want is a real problem, not a nicety
teacherNotes.note: I like a coffee, please will be understood, but I like coffee and I want a coffee mean different things and a learner who cannot separate them cannot order. Pattern 2 is the one to spend time on.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.noteType: I am hungry, not I have hunger
teacherNotes.note: A large number of languages express this with have. The correction is quick; the reason is worth giving, because it also covers thirsty, tired and cold.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.noteType: Food is personal and it is safe
teacherNotes.note: Unlike family, food is a topic every learner can speak about at length without risk, and it is the easiest place in the level to get a beginner talking. Let Speaking 2 run long if it is going well.
